newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed the week with modest losses on Friday after much-watched U.S. employment data failed to stir the torpid local market.

The U.S. added just 142,000 nonfarm jobs in April, versus predictions of a rise of near 211,000, but a drop in the unemployment rate to the lowest level in 23 years had given the report a contradictory character and muted reaction, traders said.
After a short knee-jerk trimming of early losses with Bunds, the market settled back into its range at lower levels following the data.
Business had remained slow under the influence of public holidays in the Netherlands and Europe in the last two days, one broker said.
"There is very little interest from investors in either buying or selling at the moment, and being Friday in a short week doesn't help much."
Spreads to Germany were steady, with Bund trading similarly sparse and no clear incentives to be switching between the markets at present, he added.
